summary: Adds a sentence to the Very Distant Host specification in Appendix F of BBN Report 1822: null packets do not use a channel or channel number when sent and are not acknowledged when received.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 591 supplies a sentence to add to the Very Distant Host specification. It says that a null packet uses no channel number and receives no acknowledgment.

subtitle: A sentence clarifying how the Very Distant Host specification treats null packets.

tldr.problem: The author proposed adding a sentence about null packets to the Very Distant Host specification in Appendix F of BBN Report 1822.
tldr.mechanism: The added text says that null packets use no channel or channel number when sent and are not acknowledged when received.
tldr.outcome: Readers were asked to keep this RFC with their copy of Report 1822 until that report was updated.

today: RFC 591 is a short clarification intended to be filed with BBN Report 1822 until the report is updated.

sections.title: An Addition to the Specification
sections.content: The RFC says a sentence should be added to the Very Distant Host specification in Appendix F of BBN Report 1822, in the paragraph on pages F-5 through F-7. The author asks readers to file this RFC with their copy of the report until the report is next updated.
sections.plainLanguage: The author supplies an addition for a specific paragraph in BBN Report 1822. Readers should keep the note with the report until a revised copy includes it.

sections.title: Rule for Null Packets
sections.content: The proposed sentence states: “Null packets do not use a channel (nor a channel number) when sent and are not acknowledged when received.” The note does not add other rules about packet handling.
sections.plainLanguage: A null packet is sent without a channel or channel number, and the receiver does not acknowledge it. This RFC gives that rule as a direct addition to the cited specification.

sections.title: How to Apply the Note
sections.content: RFC 591 is a small amendment intended to accompany the existing report before its next revision. It identifies the exact appendix and page range where the sentence belongs.
sections.plainLanguage: Keep the clarification alongside Report 1822 so readers can apply it to the cited section until the report is revised.
